subject: maths
title: Primary 1 Length in Centimetres
seo_title: P1 Length Worksheets: Free Primary 1 Maths on Measuring in cm with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Measuring length in centimetres; use of cm; comparing and ordering lengths; measuring and drawing a line segment to the nearest cm
meta_desc: Free P1 maths practice on length: compare longer and shorter, measure in cm with a ruler, order lengths and solve word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Put one end at 0 and count the spaces, not the marks.
key_sub: A crayon from 3 to 10 on the ruler is 10 − 3 = 7 cm long.
body_html:
Longer and shorter

To compare two things, line up one end. Then look at the other end. The one that goes further is longer. The other one is shorter.

Measure in centimetres (cm)

We measure short lengths in centimetres. We write cm. Put one end of the object at the 0 mark. Look where the other end stops. Each space between two marks is 1 cm. Count the spaces, not the marks.

If the end is between two marks, choose the nearest mark.

When the object does not start at 0

Count the spaces from where it starts to where it ends. Or subtract: end − start.

Example

A crayon starts at 2 and ends at 6. How long is it?

Count from 2: 3, 4, 5, 6 is 4 spaces. 6 − 2 = 4.

Answer: 4 cm

Draw a line

Draw a line 5 cm long.

Put a dot at 0. Draw along the ruler to 5. The line covers 5 spaces.

Answer: Stop at the 5 mark

Compare

A ribbon is 45 cm long. A string is 28 cm long. How much longer is the ribbon?

Subtract: 45 − 28 = 17. Check: 28 + 17 = 45.

Answer: 17 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Starting at 1 or at the edge of the rulerLine up the end of the object with 0
Counting the marks (7 marks for 6 cm)Count the spaces between the marks
Reading the end number when the object starts at 3Subtract the start: 10 − 3 = 7
Choosing the mark before the endChoose the nearest mark
Not lining up the ends when comparingLine up one end first
Thinking 25 cm is longer than 52 cmCompare the tens first

faq.q: What is taught in P1 length?
faq.a: Primary 1 students compare lengths, measure in centimetres with a ruler, and write cm. They also order lengths and draw a line to the nearest cm.

faq.q: How do I teach my child to use a ruler?
faq.a: Show your child how to put one end of the object at the 0 mark, then read the number where the other end stops. Ask them to count the spaces between the marks, not the marks.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when measuring length?
faq.a: The most common mistake is starting at 1, or at the edge of the ruler, instead of at 0. Children also read the end number when the object does not start at 0, and forget to line up ends.

faq.q: Is length in the MOE Primary 1 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Measuring length in centimetres, using cm, comparing and ordering lengths, and measuring and drawing a line to the nearest cm are part of Measurement in the MOE 2021 Primary 1 Mathematics syllabus.

items.q: You want to find the longer pencil. What do you do first?
items.e: Put the pencils side by side. Line up one end. Then look at the other end. The one that goes further is longer.

items.e: The ends are lined up. Look at the other ends. The worm goes the furthest. The worm is the longest.

items.q: Ahmad’s ribbon is shorter than Raju’s ribbon. Which is true?
items.e: If Ahmad’s ribbon is shorter, then Raju’s ribbon is longer. Raju’s is longer.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The crayon ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the pencil goes past it. The pencil is longer.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The straw ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the ribbon goes past it. The ribbon is longer.

items.e: The ice cream stick ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the marker goes past it. The marker is longer.

items.q: You measure with a ruler. Where do you put one end of the object?
c: at the edge of the ruler
items.e: Put the end at 0. Some rulers have a little space before the 0, so do not use the edge. If you start at 1, the number at the end is 1 too big.

items.q: How long is the eraser?
items.e: The eraser starts at 0 and ends at 2. Count the spaces: 1, 2. It is 2 cm long. There are 3 marks but only 2 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the paper clip?
items.e: The paper clip starts at 0 and ends at 3. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cm long. There are 4 marks but only 3 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the key. How long is it?
items.e: The key starts at 0 and ends at 4. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 cm long. There are 5 marks but only 4 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 5. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cm long. There are 6 marks but only 5 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the leaf?
items.e: The leaf starts at 0 and ends at 6. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. It is 6 cm long. There are 7 marks but only 6 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the caterpillar. How long is it?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 0 and ends at 7. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cm long. There are 8 marks but only 7 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: What do you count to find a length on a ruler?
c: the last number on the ruler
items.e: Each space from one mark to the next is 1 cm. Count the spaces, not the marks. A 3 cm eraser covers 3 spaces but touches 4 marks.

items.q: How long is the worm?
items.e: The worm starts at 0 and ends at 8. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. It is 8 cm long. There are 9 marks but only 8 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 9. It is 9 cm long. There are 10 marks but only 9 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the straw. How long is it?
items.e: The straw starts at 0 and ends at 10. It is 10 cm long. There are 11 marks but only 10 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the marker?
items.e: The marker starts at 0 and ends at 11. It is 11 cm long. There are 12 marks but only 11 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the ice cream stick?
items.e: The ice cream stick starts at 0 and ends at 12. It is 12 cm long. There are 13 marks but only 12 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the ribbon. How long is it?
items.e: The ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 13. It is 13 cm long. There are 14 marks but only 13 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: The end is not on a mark. About how long is the pencil?
items.e: The end is between 6 and 7. It is closer to 7. So the pencil is about 7 cm long.

items.q: The end is not on a mark. About how long is the strip of paper?
items.e: The end is between 9 and 10. It is closer to 9. So the strip of paper is about 9 cm long.

items.q: Zhi Hao drew this red line. How long is it?
items.e: The line starts at 0 and ends at 7. It covers 7 spaces, so it is 7 cm long. There are 8 marks, but count the spaces.

items.q: Mei Ling says the crayon is 7 cm long. What did she do wrong?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 6, so it is 6 cm long. Mei Ling counted 7 marks. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Hui Min wants to draw a line 6 cm long. She starts at 0. Where should she stop?
items.e: Start at 0 and draw to 6. That covers 6 spaces, so the line is 6 cm long. If you stop at 7, the line is 7 cm long.

items.q: Ethan wants a line 8 cm long. He drew this much. How many more centimetres must he draw?
items.e: The line ends at 5. Ethan needs to get to 8. Count on from 5: 6, 7, 8. That is 3 spaces. 8 − 5 = 3, so he must draw 3 cm more.

sets.title: When the object does not start at 0

items.q: Where does the crayon start?
items.e: Look at the left end of the crayon. It is at the 3 mark, not at 0. So you cannot just read the number at the other end.

items.q: How long is the eraser?
items.e: The eraser starts at 1, not at 0. Count on from 1: 2, 3, 4. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 4 − 1 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 4 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The crayon does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The crayon starts at 2, not at 0. Count on from 2: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. That is 5 spaces. Or subtract: 7 − 2 = 5. So it is 5 cm long. 7 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the key?
items.e: The key starts at 3, not at 0. Count on from 3: 4, 5, 6. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 6 − 3 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 6 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The leaf does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The leaf starts at 1, not at 0. Subtract: 8 − 1 = 7. So it is 7 cm long. 8 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Kumar says the crayon is 9 cm long. What did he do wrong?
items.e: The crayon starts at 1, not at 0, so 9 is too big. 9 − 1 = 8. The crayon is 8 cm long.

items.q: How long is the caterpillar?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 4, not at 0. Count on from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 5 spaces. Or subtract: 9 − 4 = 5. So it is 5 cm long. 9 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The paper clip does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The paper clip starts at 5, not at 0. Count on from 5: 6, 7, 8. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 8 − 5 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 8 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the marker?
items.e: The marker starts at 2, not at 0. Subtract: 10 − 2 = 8. So it is 8 cm long. 10 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The end of Farah’s ruler is broken. It starts at 4. A paper clip goes from 4 to 7. How long is it?
items.e: Count from 4, not from 0: 5, 6, 7 is 3 spaces. 7 − 4 = 3, so the paper clip is 3 cm long.

items.q: The worm does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The worm starts at 6, not at 0. Subtract: 13 − 6 = 7. So it is 7 cm long. 13 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the straw?
items.e: The straw starts at 3, not at 0. Subtract: 12 − 3 = 9. So it is 9 cm long. 12 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Priya measures a key. One end is at 5. The other end is at 9. How long is the key?
items.e: The key starts at 5, not at 0. Count the spaces from 5 to 9: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4. Or subtract: 9 − 5 = 4. The key is 4 cm long.

items.q: The pencil does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The pencil starts at 1, not at 0. Subtract: 11 − 1 = 10. So it is 10 cm long. 11 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: A pencil goes from 3 to 12 on a ruler. Ali counts the marks and gets 10. How long is the pencil?
items.e: Count spaces, not marks. From 3 to 12 there are 10 marks but only 9 spaces. 12 − 3 = 9, so the pencil is 9 cm long.

items.q: How long is the ice cream stick?
items.e: The ice cream stick starts at 5, not at 0. Subtract: 14 − 5 = 9. So it is 9 cm long. 14 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The ribbon does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The ribbon starts at 4, not at 0. Subtract: 15 − 4 = 11. So it is 11 cm long. 15 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Look at the crayon and the key. Which is true?
items.e: The crayon goes from 0 to 5: 5 cm. The key goes from 3 to 8: 8 − 3 = 5 cm. They are the same length. The key ends at a bigger number, but it also starts later.

items.q: Nurul starts a line at 4. She draws it 6 cm long. Where does the line end?
items.e: Start at 4 and count 6 spaces: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Or add: 4 + 6 = 10. The line ends at 10.

items.q: Devi starts a line at 2. She wants it to be 7 cm long. Where should she stop?
items.e: Start at 2 and count 7 spaces: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Or add: 2 + 7 = 9. Stop at 9. If you stop at 7, the line is only 5 cm long.

sets.title: Compare and order lengths in cm

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: The pencil is 9 cm. The crayon is 6 cm. 9 is more than 6. The pencil is longer.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: The straw is 7 cm. The marker is 11 cm. 7 is less than 11. The straw is shorter.

items.q: How much longer is the pencil than the crayon?
items.e: Both start at 0. The pencil ends at 12. The crayon ends at 7. 12 − 7 = 5. The pencil is 5 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the straw than the eraser?
items.e: Both start at 0. The straw ends at 10. The eraser ends at 3. 10 − 3 = 7. The straw is 7 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the ribbon than the key?
items.e: Both start at 0. The ribbon ends at 13. The key ends at 6. 13 − 6 = 7. The ribbon is 7 cm longer.

items.q: How much shorter is the crayon than the pencil?
items.e: The pencil is 9 cm. The crayon is 4 cm. 9 − 4 = 5. The crayon is 5 cm shorter.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: The straw goes from 0 to 7: 7 cm. The pencil goes from 5 to 11: 11 − 5 = 6 cm. The straw is longer, even though the pencil ends at a bigger number.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: The marker goes from 0 to 5: 5 cm. The ice cream stick goes from 3 to 12: 12 − 3 = 9 cm. 9 is more than 5, so the ice cream stick is longer.

items.q: Order them from shortest to longest.
items.e: The key is 4 cm, the crayon is 6 cm and the pencil is 10 cm. Shortest first: key, crayon, pencil.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: The straw is 8 cm, the marker is 11 cm and the eraser is 3 cm. 11 is the biggest number, so the marker is the longest.

items.q: Which ribbon is the longest?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 2 tens, 4 tens, 3 tens, 1 ten. Ribbon B is 42 cm, so Ribbon B is the longest.

items.q: Which ribbon is the shortest?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 3 tens, 1 ten, 2 tens, 3 tens. Ribbon B is 13 cm, so Ribbon B is the shortest.

items.q: Which ribbon is shorter than 20 cm?
items.e: 20 has 2 tens. Ribbon C is 12 cm. 12 has only 1 ten, so Ribbon C is shorter than 20 cm. 21 cm is a little longer than 20 cm.

items.q: Order the strips from longest to shortest.
items.e: 52 cm is the longest. 38 cm is next. 25 cm is the shortest. Longest first: A, C, B. Do not order by the ones: 25 has 2 tens, so it is the shortest.

items.q: Order the strips from shortest to longest.
items.e: 47 cm has 4 tens, 60 cm has 6 tens and 74 cm has 7 tens. Shortest first: A, C, B.

items.q: Whose string is longer?
items.e: 46 has 4 tens. 64 has 6 tens. 6 tens is more, so Siti’s string is longer. Same digits, but the tens are different.

items.q: Which length is the longest?
items.e: Compare the tens first. 83 and 80 both have 8 tens. Then compare the ones: 3 is more than 0. So 83 cm is the longest.

items.q: Which length is shorter than 25 cm?
items.e: 19 has 1 ten. 25 has 2 tens. So 19 cm is shorter. 25 cm is not shorter than 25 cm. It is the same.

items.q: 47 cm is ____ than 74 cm.
items.e: 47 has 4 tens. 74 has 7 tens. 47 is less than 74, so 47 cm is shorter.

items.q: Order from shortest to longest: 61 cm, 16 cm, 60 cm
items.e: 16 has only 1 ten, so it is the shortest. 60 and 61 both have 6 tens. 0 ones is less than 1 one. So the order is 16 cm, 60 cm, 61 cm.

items.q: Sarah’s ribbon is 14 cm long. Wei Ming’s ribbon is 9 cm long. How much longer is Sarah’s ribbon?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract: 14 − 9 = 5 cm. Or count on from 9 to 14: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. Do not add. 14 + 9 = 23 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Chloe’s pencil was 17 cm long. She sharpened it. Now it is 12 cm. How much shorter is it?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract: 17 − 12 = 5 cm. Or count on from 12 to 17: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. Do not add. 17 + 12 = 29 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Hafiz’s bean plant was 8 cm tall. It grew 5 cm more. How tall is it now?
items.e: It grew, so add: 8 + 5 = 13 cm. Count on from 8: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13.

items.q: Ryan puts two ice cream sticks end to end. Each is 11 cm long. How long are they together?
items.e: Add the two lengths: 11 + 11 = 22 cm.

items.q: Kumar drew this line. Then he made it 4 cm longer. How long is the line now?
items.e: The line is 5 cm. Add 4 cm more: 5 + 4 = 9 cm. It now ends at 9.

items.q: At East Coast Park, Devi found this worm and caterpillar. How much longer is the worm?
items.e: The worm is 9 cm. The caterpillar is 4 cm. 9 − 4 = 5 cm.

items.q: Ali’s pencil case is 20 cm long. His pencil is 17 cm long. How much longer is the pencil case?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract: 20 − 17 = 3 cm. Or count on from 17 to 20: 18, 19, 20. Do not add. 20 + 17 = 37 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Xin Yi joins two paper strips end to end. How long is the long strip now?
items.e: Joining end to end makes it longer, so add: 24 + 15 = 39 cm. 2 tens + 1 ten = 3 tens. 4 + 5 = 9 ones.

items.q: Farah joins 3 ribbons end to end. Each ribbon is 10 cm long. How long is the long ribbon?
items.e: Count in tens: 10, 20, 30. Or add: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 cm.

items.q: A bubble tea straw is 21 cm long. A small straw is 15 cm long. How much longer is the bubble tea straw?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract: 21 − 15 = 6 cm. Or count on from 15 to 21: 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21. Do not add. 21 + 15 = 36 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: At the hawker centre, Arjun’s chopstick is 23 cm long. His spoon is 14 cm long. How much shorter is the spoon?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract: 23 − 14 = 9 cm. Check: 14 + 9 = 23. Do not add. 23 + 14 = 37 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Ethan says the pencil is 11 cm long. How long is it really?
items.e: The pencil starts at 2, not at 0. Ethan read the end number. 11 − 2 = 9 cm.

items.q: Ali, Siti and Raju each grow a plant. Whose plant is the tallest?
items.e: Compare the tens: 34 has 3 tens, 43 has 4 tens, 29 has 2 tens. 43 cm is the most. Siti’s plant is the tallest.

items.q: For Chinese New Year, Mrs Lim cuts a red strip 45 cm long and a gold strip 30 cm long. How much longer is the red strip?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract: 45 − 30 = 15 cm. Check: 30 + 15 = 45. Do not add. 45 + 30 = 75 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Ahmad needs 60 cm of ribbon. He has 45 cm. How many more centimetres does he need?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract: 60 − 45 = 15 cm. Check: 45 + 15 = 60.

items.q: Jun Jie has a ribbon 50 cm long. He cuts off 18 cm for a Children’s Day card. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Take away the part cut off: 50 − 18 = 32 cm. Rename 5 tens as 4 tens 10 ones. 10 − 8 = 2, 4 − 1 = 3. Check: 18 + 32 = 50.

items.q: Raju’s hair ribbon is 28 cm long. Zhi Hao’s hair ribbon is 9 cm longer. How long is Zhi Hao’s ribbon?
items.e: “Longer” means more, so add: 28 + 9 = 37 cm. 8 + 9 = 17 ones. Rename 10 ones as 1 ten.

items.q: Mei Ling’s string is 52 cm long. Hui Min’s string is 15 cm shorter. How long is Hui Min’s string?
items.e: “Shorter” means less, so subtract: 52 − 15 = 37 cm. Rename 5 tens 2 ones as 4 tens 12 ones. 12 − 5 = 7, 4 − 1 = 3.

items.q: Nurul makes a paper chain for National Day. One part is 45 cm. The other part is 38 cm. She joins them. How long is the chain?
items.e: Joining makes it longer, so add: 45 + 38 = 83 cm. 5 + 8 = 13 ones. Rename 10 ones as 1 ten. 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 tens.

items.q: Kavya has a ribbon 60 cm long. She uses 30 cm for a bow. She uses 12 cm for a card. How much is left?
